## PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.3 GRADES OF CONCRETE
- A. Concrete Grade Designations and corresponding required characteristic compressive strength in the Work shall be as shown in Table 4.

## PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.3 GRADES OF CONCRETE > TABLE -- 4 / CONCRETE GRADES AND CHARACTERISTIC COMPRESSIVE STRENGTHS
[IS 456 - TABLE 2]

| GRADE DESIGNATION   | SPECIFIED CHARACTERISTIC COMPRESSIVE STRENGTH [N/mm 2 ] AT 28 DAYS   |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1                   | 2 [N/mm 2 ]                                                          |
| M 10                | 10                                                                   |
| M 15                | 15                                                                   |
| M 20                | 20                                                                   |
| M 25                | 25                                                                   |
| M 30                | 30                                                                   |
| M 35                | 35                                                                   |
| M 40                | 40                                                                   |
| M 60                | 60                                                                   |

- NOTE - 1 In the designation of a concrete of mix, letter M refers to the mix and the number to the specified characteristic compressive strength of 15 cm cube at 28 days, expressed in N/mm 2 .
- NOTE - 2 M 5 and M 7.5 grade of concrete may be used for lean concrete bases and simple foundations for masonry walls. These mixes need not be designed.
- NOTE - 3 Grades of concrete lower than M 15 shall not be used in reinforced concrete.

## PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.4 DURABILITY AND COMPATIBILITY REQUIREMENTS FOR CONCRETE AND MATERIALS

- NOTE - 1 When the maximum water cement ratio can be strictly controlled, the cement content in the above table may be reduced by 10 percent.
- NOTE - 2 The minimum cement content is based on 20 mm, aggregate. For 40 mm aggregate, it should be reduced by about 10 percent; for 12.5 mm aggregate, it should be increased by about 10 percent.
